abstract: As plant genome resources expand, updating established annotations requires incorporating improved gene models without disrupting correct structures or stable identifiers. We developed GeneArbiter, an evidence guided framework that treats annotation updating as a correction preservation problem. GeneArbiter uses the current annotation as a backbone, integrates alternative models with RNA splice junction and homologous protein evidence, and applies constrained language model arbitration followed by deterministic release and identifier reconciliation. In rice MH63, GeneArbiter recovered 4,701 reference loci missed by the current annotation while losing 1,890 current exact loci, yielding a net gain of 2,811 exact matches and increasing the gene level exact hit rate from 70.77% to 77.77%. It retained 97.54% of protein coding genes in the mature TAIR12 annotation and improved protein set quality metrics across 16 plant genomes. Independent transcript and protein evidence further supported GeneArbiter selected structural revisions at reference discordant loci. These results establish GeneArbiter as a conservative and traceable framework for maintaining plant genome annotations as new predictions and biological evidence accumulate.
